record.original_question: Develop a theory of k-orbit realizations of m-orbit polytopes.

evidence.quote: Problem 33. Develop a theory of k-orbit realizations of m-orbit polytopes.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An abstract polytope is a partially ordered set whose elements (called faces) satisfy the standard combinatorial axioms of an abstract polytope: it is ranked, has unique minimum and maximum faces, every maximal chain (flag) contains exactly one face of each rank, it is strongly flag-connected, and it satisfies the diamond condition. The automorphism group of an abstract polytope acts freely on the set of flags; the polytope is called an m-orbit polytope if this action has exactly m orbits on flags. A (geometric) realization of an abstract polytope P is a mapping β from the vertex set of P into some Euclidean space such that every automorphism of P is induced by an isometry of the ambient space; the realization extends to all faces, and the symmetry group of the realized figure acts on its flags. The realization is called a k-orbit realization if the symmetry group of the resulting geometric figure has exactly k orbits on the flags of P.

Develop a systematic theory of k-orbit realizations of m-orbit abstract polytopes. In particular, for given integers k and m, characterize which m-orbit abstract polytopes admit a faithful k-orbit realization in some Euclidean space, describe the structure of the cone (or space) of all such realizations, determine the possible relationships k ↔ m (including necessary divisibility or group-theoretic conditions linking the symmetry groups of realizations to the abstract automorphism group), and provide existence and classification results for the realizations whose flag-orbit count differs from the abstract flag-orbit count.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears in a list of 35 open problems on k-orbit abstract polytopes published in Discrete Mathematics (Pellicer, 2018). Subsequent literature on k-orbit polytopes and realizations (e.g., work on 2-orbit and 3-orbit polyhedra, characterizations of automorphism groups of k-orbit polytopes, and combining realization space models of polytopes) addresses related aspects but no comprehensive theory of k-orbit realizations of m-orbit polytopes has been established. The status appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Finite 3-Orbit Polyhedra in Ordinary Space I
